analyst.summary: Patanjali Foods combines a large, price-volatile edible oils business (volumes roughly flat to slightly down) with a growing branded FMCG portfolio under the Patanjali name. A steep stock price decline over the past year appears to be driving a Sell signal in our quantitative model, but the underlying fundamentals tell a more balanced story: the company has meaningfully reduced debt over several years, returns on capital are respectable, and the valuation (under 20x earnings) is not demanding. A recent margin dip looks tied to edible-oil price swings rather than a structural problem, though a wheat-flour quality recall and a minor tax penalty are worth watching. On balance, we see this as a Hold rather than a name to exit.
